name: Heavy Chain Disease

criteria.description: Detection of monoclonal heavy chain proteins in serum or urine by immunofixation electrophoresis
Bone marrow biopsy showing infiltration by abnormal plasma cells producing truncated heavy chains
Presence of clinical symptoms such as lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or constitutional symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of monoclonal heavy chain protein plus bone marrow plasma cell infiltration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on laboratory detection of abnormal heavy chains and histopathology; no universally accepted diagnostic criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal truncated immunoglobulin heavy chain proteinuria
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic presence of abnormal heavy chain proteins in urine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Monoclonal truncated immunoglobulin heavy chain proteinemia
pathognomonic.notes: Serum detection of abnormal heavy chain proteins

common.notes: Reduced hemoglobin levels due to marrow infiltration

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms (weight loss, fever, night sweats)
searchTerms: constitutional symptoms like fatigue and fever

occasional.notes: Nerve involvement causing sensory or motor deficits
Kidney dysfunction secondary to heavy chain deposition
Cutaneous manifestations reported in some cases

rare.notes: Rare deposition of amyloid in cardiac tissue

laboratory: Serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis showing monoclonal truncated heavy chains
Bone marrow biopsy with clonal plasma cell infiltration
Elevated serum free heavy chain levels
imaging: CT or ultrasound showing lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly
MRI or echocardiography if cardiac amyloidosis suspected
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations in plasma cells may be present
other: Histopathological confirmation of truncated heavy chain deposits in tissues
Flow cytometry showing abnormal plasma cell populations

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of intact monoclonal immunoglobulins rather than truncated heavy chains
Higher plasma cell burden in bone marrow
Monoclonal light chains detected instead of heavy chains
Different clinical presentation and laboratory findings
Absence of monoclonal heavy chain proteins

redFlags: Rapidly progressive anemia with bone marrow failure
Severe renal impairment due to heavy chain deposition
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Kyle RA, Rajkumar SV. Heavy chain diseases. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 1999;13(6):1243-1258.
